narrative.intro: Flightsafety Defense shows concentrated federal activity in FY2026 to date. Flightsafety Defense obligated $665M across 6 awards, with an average award size of $111M and year-over-year change up 778.1%. Flightsafety Defense moved from single-digit tens of millions in prior fiscal years to a much larger FY2026 total: FY21 obligations were $78.9M, FY22 obligations were $74.2M, FY23 obligations were $99.7M, FY24 obligations were $81.3M, and FY25 obligations were $75.7M. Flightsafety Defense sells mainly into aerospace-related NAICS codes, with Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing accounting for $641M and Flight Training accounting for $23.8M in FY2026 to date. Flightsafety Defense’s current-year totals are partial because FY2026 is fiscal year to date. Flightsafety Defense’s profile shows a shift in scale this fiscal year concentrated in aircraft parts and training markets, reflected in the headline totals and the industry breakdown.
